lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine just started a new chapter: a software developer internship at La Caisse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Digital and Analytics Solutions group, working on development and business-process automation.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does the day-to-day look like?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: According to his CV entry, which starts in August 2026, three things. Automating business processes with SharePoint, TypeScript, C sharp and dot NET. Contributing to A P I integrations and to the migration away from SnapLogic. And working with a cross-functional team to turn business needs into application and integration requirements.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So it's code, plumbing and requirements.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's how he describes it. The mix of software, system integration and requirements work he was looking for, the same shape as his earlier platform and backend roles, but in an institutional setting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's he carrying over from before?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Platform and CI/CD discipline from the IMC2 secure cloud work, with GitLab pipelines, GKE and Terraform. Teaching and documentation habits from Polytechnique and ÉTS, like reproducible setups and clear hand-offs. And dot NET plus structured error handling from IONODES, where Serilog and Sentry fed production diagnostics.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I like that he lists habits and not just tools.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a human detail too. He names three people who welcomed him onto the team, and says the offices carry a lot of Quebec art.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds like a good first impression.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The full post has the details and links back to those earlier roles.
